1: # Clean the order export
2: 
3: Our shop exports orders as a messy CSV (see `orders_raw.csv`). Write `clean.py` so that
4: 
5:     python3 clean.py INPUT.csv OUTPUT.csv
6: 
7: writes a clean CSV. It will be run on other exports with the same kinds of mess, so do not
8: hardcode anything about this particular file. Python 3.9, standard library only.
9: 
10: ## Input
11: - May start with a UTF-8 BOM. Blank lines and lines whose first character is `#` are ignored.
12: - Header names are matched after trimming, lowercasing and turning spaces into `_`
13:   (so ` Order ID` → `order_id`). Columns may come in any order. Extra columns are ignored.
14: - Columns: `order_id, customer_email, amount, currency, order_date, status, updated_at`.
15: - Every value may have surrounding whitespace; trim it.
16: 
17: ## Rules per field
18: - **order_id**: trimmed, uppercased. Rows with an empty order_id are dropped.
19: - **customer_email**: trimmed, lowercased. If it does not contain exactly one `@` with
20:   non-empty text on both sides, output an empty string (keep the row).
21: - **amount**: may contain a currency symbol (`$`, `€`, `£`) anywhere, spaces, thousands
22:   separators, and accounting negatives in parentheses: `(12.50)` = -12.50.
23:   Decimal separator rule: if both `.` and `,` appear, whichever appears **last** is the decimal
24:   separator and the other is a thousands separator. If only `,` appears and exactly two digits
25:   follow the last `,`, it is the decimal separator; otherwise `,` is a thousands separator.
26:   If only `.` appears it is the decimal separator.
27:   Output with exactly 2 decimals, rounding half away from zero (`2.005` → `2.01`).
28:   Rows with an empty or unparseable amount are dropped.
29: - **currency**: trimmed, uppercased. `$` → `USD`, `€` → `EUR`, `£` → `GBP`. If the currency
30:   field is empty, take it from a symbol in the amount; if there is none, use `USD`.
31: - **order_date**: output `YYYY-MM-DD`. Accepted inputs:
32:   `2026-03-04`, `2026/03/04`, `04.03.2026` (day.month.year), `03/04/2026` (month/day/year),
33:   `Mar 4, 2026` / `March 4, 2026`, `4 Mar 2026` / `4 March 2026` (English month names,
34:   any case). Single-digit day/month allowed in numeric forms. Rows with a missing or invalid
35:   date (e.g. `2026-02-30`) are dropped.
36: - **status**: trimmed, lowercased; `canceled` → `cancelled`. Allowed: `pending, paid, shipped,
37:   cancelled, refunded`. Anything else becomes `unknown`.
38: - **updated_at**: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` optionally followed by `Z`, or the same with a space
39:   instead of `T`. Only used for de-duplication; not in the output. Empty = oldest possible.
40: 
41: ## De-duplication
42: Rows with the same (normalised) order_id: keep only the one with the latest `updated_at`.
43: On a tie, keep the one that appears later in the file. Dropped rows (bad amount/date/id) never
44: take part in de-duplication.
45: 
46: ## Output
47: Header `order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status`, then rows sorted by
48: `order_date`, then `order_id`. Standard `csv` module quoting, `\n` line endings.

# spec-check

Mistakes I keep seeing on these jobs, and what to do instead.

## 1. Finishing without running anything
"I did not run the script" is a failed job. Before you stop:
- Turn **every example in the spec** into an assert and run it. Copy them verbatim.
- If there is a sample input file, run your code on it and read every output row.
- Run the existing tests, if any.

## 2. Being lenient where the spec is strict
If the spec lists the accepted forms, the list is closed. Everything else is invalid.
- `Mar 4, 2026` allowed does **not** mean `Mar 4 2026` is allowed.
- Don't reach for forgiving parsers (`dateutil`, `strptime` with fallbacks, `float()`,
  `int()` on untrimmed text). Write a strict pattern per allowed form and use `re.fullmatch`.
- Read notes/comments in sample data: rows marked "bad" are telling you something.

## 3. Only testing the happy path

(wrong case, extra space, missing part, out of range, wrong order, wrong type).

When the spec examples and your negative cases pass, stop. Don't keep deliberating.

import csv, io, os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/<path>')
import clean

# --- helpers ---
def val(**kw):
    header = ["order_id","customer_email","amount","currency","order_date","status","updated_at"]
    row = [kw.get(h, "") for h in header]
    idx = {h:i for i,h in enumerate(header)}
    return clean.clean_row(row, idx)

# header normalisation examples
assert clean.normalize_header(" Order ID ") == "order_id"
assert clean.normalize_header("Customer Email") == "customer_email"
assert clean.normalize_header("UPDATED_AT") == "updated_at"

# amount examples from spec
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("(12.50)")
assert a == "-12.50" and cur is None
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("2.005")
assert a == "2.01"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("$1,234.50")
assert a == "1234.50" and cur == "USD"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("1.234,56")
assert a == "1234.56"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("1,000")
assert a == "1000.00"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("€ 7,5")
assert a == "75.00" and cur == "EUR"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("(1,000.005)")
assert a == "-1000.01"
for bad in ["", "   ", "abc", "1.2.3", "1..2", "(1.2", "12.3)"]:
    assert clean.parse_amount(bad) is None, bad

# email
assert clean.valid_email("<email>") == "<email>"
assert clean.valid_email("a@@b.com") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("@b.com") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("a@") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("ab.com") == ""

# dates: all accepted forms
accepted = {
    "2026-03-04":"2026-03-04",
    "2026/03/04":"2026-03-04",
    "04.03.2026":"2026-03-04",
    "03/04/2026":"2026-03-04",
    "Mar 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "March 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "4 Mar 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "4 March 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "2026-3-4":"2026-03-04",
    "mAr 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
}
for src, expected in accepted.items():
    got = clean.parse_date(src)
    assert got is not None and got.isoformat() == expected, (src, got)
rejected_dates = ["", "2026-02-30", "Mar 4 2026", "2026-13-01", "13/04/2026", "04-03-2026", "February 30, 2026"]
for src in rejected_dates:
    assert clean.parse_date(src) is None, src

# status
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="Cancelled")["status"] == "cancelled"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="canceled")["status"] == "cancelled"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="PAID")["status"] == "paid"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="lost")["status"] == "unknown"

# updated_at
from datetime import datetime
assert clean.parse_updated_at("2026-03-04T10:00:00Z") == datetime(2026,3,4,10,0,0)
assert clean.parse_updated_at("2026-03-04 10:00:00") == datetime(2026,3,4,10,0,0)
assert clean.parse_updated_at("") == datetime.min
assert clean.parse_updated_at("nonsense") == datetime.min

# full pipeline via temp files
inp = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
with open(inp, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
    f.write(" Order ID ,Customer Email,Amount,Currency,Order Date,Status,Updated At,Notes\n")
    f.write("# comment\n\n")
    f.write("a-1, <email> ,(12.50),,Mar 4, 2026,PAID,2026-03-04T10:00:00Z,x\n")
    f.write("A-1,<email>,3,,2026-03-04,paid,2026-03-04T10:00:00Z,tie-later\n")
    f.write("a-2,,$5,,2026-03-05,canceled,,y\n")
    f.write("a-3,,,,\n")
    f.write("a-4,,bad,,2026-03-05,paid,,\n")
    f.write("a-5,,5,,2026-02-30,paid,,\n")
    f.write("a-6,,5,,2026-03-05,paid,2026-03-06T00:00:00,\n")
    f.write("a-6,,6,,2026-03-05,paid,2026-03-06T00:00:00,later-tie\n")
clean.main(["clean.py", inp, out])
with open(out, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    data = f.read()
assert data == (
    "order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status\n"
    "A-1,<email>,3.00,USD,2026-03-04,paid\n"
    "A-2,,5.00,USD,2026-03-05,cancelled\n"
    "A-6,,6.00,USD,2026-03-05,paid\n"
), data
os.remove(inp); os.remove(out)
print("ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED")

assert clean.normalize_header(" Order ID ") == "order_id"
assert clean.normalize_header("Customer Email") == "customer_email"
assert clean.normalize_header("UPDATED_AT") == "updated_at"

# amount examples from spec
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("(12.50)")
assert a == "-12.50" and cur is None
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("2.005")
assert a == "2.01"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("$1,234.50")
assert a == "1234.50" and cur == "USD"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("1.234,56")
assert a == "1234.56"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("1,000")
assert a == "1000.00"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("€ 7,5")
assert a == "75.00" and cur == "EUR"
a, cur = clean.parse_amount("(1,000.005)")
assert a == "-1000.01"
for bad in ["", "   ", "abc", "1.2.3", "1..2", "(1.2", "12.3)"]:
    assert clean.parse_amount(bad) is None, bad

# email
assert clean.valid_email("<email>") == "<email>"
assert clean.valid_email("a@@b.com") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("@b.com") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("a@") == ""
assert clean.valid_email("ab.com") == ""

# dates: all accepted forms
accepted = {
    "2026-03-04":"2026-03-04",
    "2026/03/04":"2026-03-04",
    "04.03.2026":"2026-03-04",
    "03/04/2026":"2026-03-04",
    "Mar 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "March 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "4 Mar 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "4 March 2026":"2026-03-04",
    "2026-3-4":"2026-03-04",
    "mAr 4, 2026":"2026-03-04",
}
for src, expected in accepted.items():
    got = clean.parse_date(src)
    assert got is not None and got.isoformat() == expected, (src, got)
rejected_dates = ["", "2026-02-30", "Mar 4 2026", "2026-13-01", "13/04/2026", "04-03-2026", "February 30, 2026"]
for src in rejected_dates:
    assert clean.parse_date(src) is None, src

# status
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="Cancelled")["status"] == "cancelled"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="canceled")["status"] == "cancelled"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="PAID")["status"] == "paid"
assert val(order_id="a", amount="1", order_date="2026-03-04", status="lost")["status"] == "unknown"

# updated_at
from datetime import datetime
assert clean.parse_updated_at("2026-03-04T10:00:00Z") == datetime(2026,3,4,10,0,0)
assert clean.parse_updated_at("2026-03-04 10:00:00") == datetime(2026,3,4,10,0,0)
assert clean.parse_updated_at("") == datetime.min
assert clean.parse_updated_at("nonsense") == datetime.min

# full pipeline via temp files
inp = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
with open(inp, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
    f.write(" Order ID ,Customer Email,Amount,Currency,Order Date,Status,Updated At,Notes\n")
    f.write("# comment\n\n")
    f.write("a-1, <email> ,(12.50),,Mar 4, 2026,PAID,2026-03-04T10:00:00Z,x\n")
    f.write("A-1,<email>,3,,2026-03-04,paid,2026-03-04T10:00:00Z,tie-later\n")
    f.write("a-2,,$5,,2026-03-05,canceled,,y\n")
    f.write("a-3,,,,\n")
    f.write("a-4,,bad,,2026-03-05,paid,,\n")
    f.write("a-5,,5,,2026-02-30,paid,,\n")
    f.write("a-6,,5,,2026-03-05,paid,2026-03-06T00:00:00,\n")
    f.write("a-6,,6,,2026-03-05,paid,2026-03-06T00:00:00,later-tie\n")
clean.main(["clean.py", inp, out])
with open(out, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    data = f.read()
assert data == (
    "order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status\n"
    "A-1,<email>,3.00,USD,2026-03-04,paid\n"
    "A-2,,5.00,USD,2026-03-05,cancelled\n"
    "A-6,,6.00,USD,2026-03-05,paid\n"
), data
os.remove(inp); os.remove(out)
print("ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED")

part.text:
Implemented `clean.py` in the project directory. It handles BOM/comments, reordered headers, field trimming, amount parsing and rounding, currency inference, all specified date formats, status normalization, `updated_at` de-duplication, and sorted CSV output with `\n` endings.

Verified against the sample export and a test suite covering every spec example plus invalid/malformed cases. Sample output:

```csv
order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status
A-1001,alice@example.com,1300.00,USD,2026-03-04,refunded
A-1002,bob@example.com,99.00,USD,2026-03-04,shipped
A-1003,,1234.56,EUR,2026-03-04,cancelled
A-1006,frank@example.com,75.00,EUR,2026-03-07,pending
A-1007,gina@example,3.10,GBP,2026-03-09,unknown
A-1008,hank@example.com,1000.00,GBP,2026-03-10,paid
A-1010,jack@example.com,-1000.01,USD,2026-03-10,paid
```
